security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI CSR save/restore code (e.g., HSM suspend/resume or domain context switch) accesses CSR mseccfgh on an RV64 hart where the CSR is not defined, or uses an XLEN-agnostic CSR_READ/CSR_WRITE macro for mseccfgh without a __riscv_xlen == 32 guard.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR_READ(CSR_MSECCFGH) or CSR_WRITE(CSR_MSECCFGH) without #if __riscv_xlen == 32 preprocessor guard, or a generic __ASM_STR(mseccfgh) string in inline asm that compiles unconditionally for both RV32 and RV64 targets.
security_spec.summary: Unconditional mseccfgh access on RV64 triggers an illegal instruction trap in M-mode, crashing OpenSBI irrecoverably because M-mode has no higher privilege to handle the fault.

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFGH (0x757) is defined unconditionally without an __riscv_xlen==32 preprocessor guard. While the definition is currently unused by any code path, its unprotected presence means any future code that references CSR_MSECCFGH via CSR_READ/CSR_WRITE on an RV64 hart will assemble to an illegal CSR access (0x757 is RV32-only). The definition should either be guarded with #if __riscv_xlen == 32 or removed entirely since no code currently uses it.

HSM non-retentive suspend save only preserves mie, mip (SSIP/STIP), medeleg, mideleg, and menvcfg. CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) is not saved, meaning SSEED/USEED/RLB/MML/MMWP bits configured during init are lost across suspend/resume. On RV32, CSR_MSECCFGH would also need saving if the register is implemented. No saved_mseccfg field exists in struct sbi_hsm_data.

HSM non-retentive suspend restore writes back menvcfg, mideleg, medeleg, mie, and mip but never writes CSR_MSECCFG. The mseccfg register retains whatever value the warm-boot init sequence assigns (via mstatus_init -> csr_set/clear on SSEED/USEED, and sbi_hart_protection_configure -> csr_set on RLB/MML). Any runtime modifications to mseccfg made after init by S-mode are silently discarded on resume.
